title: Can we use phone number as the primary info used to authenticate users instead of email?

posts.name: Clament John
posts.cooked:
I see many discussions requesting a way to let users log in using their phone number. While most people mean authenticating with just a phone number and OTP, the solutions shared by the community often involve using the phone number alongside an email address for authentication.

I’m planning to use ERPNext in India, where most people are mobile-first rather than email-first. A native way to let users - including my staff, customers, and vendors - authenticate using just their phone number and OTP would offer a much better experience than requiring an email address first and then optionally adding a phone number later.

Here are a few discussions I found that didn’t quite provide the solution I was looking for:

Here are a few discussions I found without the answer I was looking for

  1. How to make the user sign up with mobile number instead of email

In this discussion, the suggested solution is to enable “Allow Login using Mobile Number” in the settings. However, this only allows users to use their mobile number at the login step and does not eliminate the requirement to have an email address to begin with.

  1. Login with Mobile and OTP

Here the solution is to use a custom whitelisted function (code provided at agrinext/agrinext/otp.py at develop · agrinext/agrinext · GitHub) which can authenticate using phone + OTP. But this still needs the user to have a valid email address to create the account.

Is there a better solution?
